thesis: C3.ai, Inc. (NYSE: AI) sells enterprise application software for artificial intelligence: a model-driven platform used to build, deploy, and operate predictive and generative AI applications for large organizations. **[Fact]** The company reports as a single operating segment. **[Fact]** FY2026 revenue (year ended April 30, 2026) was **$227.1 million**, down from **$327.6 million** in FY2025 per XBRL-tagged filing extracts. **[Fact]** Cash and cash equivalents were **$66.2 million** with **no reported long-term debt** at the April 30, 2026 balance sheet date. **[Inference]** C3.ai is an application-layer enterprise AI vendor competing with hyperscaler platforms and specialized software peers; owner economics today depend on converting large-deal pipeline into durable subscription revenue without further dilution.
why_market_wrong: The market may be overweighting **CEO Thomas Siebel's return**, **Federal and Shell partnership headlines**, and **insider purchase activity** while underweighting a **31% revenue decline**, **unproven switching-cost moat** against hyperscalers, and **stock-based compensation dilution**. **[Inference]** At **$8.61** (Yahoo close 2026-07-20), the stock embeds recovery in normalized owner cash that filings have not yet confirmed: our base case uses **$0.80 per share** starting owner cash **[Assumption]**, not the spot GAAP earnings path. **[Inference]** The universal contract sums four non-overlapping components (platform cash engine, pipeline runway, net cash, dilution reserve) to **$20.98 per share** base value; if revenue stabilizes and Federal deals convert, upside exists, but moat durability remains the binding gate.
